## SV-CKE-001: Session-like cookie without HttpOnly (v1)

A response set a cookie whose name matches the documented session-cookie heuristic, without the HttpOnly attribute. Whether it is a session identifier needs to be verified.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** low / medium / manual_verification_required
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** A cookie whose name matches the session heuristic was set without HttpOnly.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That it is a session token; that script injection exists; that it can be stolen.
- **Remediation:** If the cookie identifies a session or carries credentials, set HttpOnly so scripts cannot read it.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-SESS-02 Testing for Cookies Attributes
- **CWE:** CWE-1004 Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag

## SV-CKE-002: Cookie set over HTTPS without Secure (v1)

A response delivered over HTTPS set a cookie without the Secure attribute.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** low / high / automated_detection
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** A cookie was set by an HTTPS response without Secure.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That an HTTP endpoint exists or is reachable; that the cookie is sensitive.
- **Remediation:** Set the Secure attribute on cookies issued over HTTPS.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-SESS-02 Testing for Cookies Attributes
- **CWE:** CWE-614 Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

## SV-CKE-003: Cookie without a SameSite attribute (v1)

A cookie was set without a SameSite attribute, so cross-site behaviour depends on browser defaults.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** informational / high / automated_detection
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** A cookie was set without a SameSite attribute.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** Browser behaviour (defaults differ between browsers); that any request-forgery attack is possible.
- **Remediation:** Set an explicit SameSite attribute (Lax or Strict where possible).
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** none
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-SESS-02 Testing for Cookies Attributes
- **CWE:** CWE-1275 Sensitive Cookie with Improper SameSite Attribute

## SV-COR-001: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * returned (v1)

Responses returned Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, allowing any origin to read them from a browser. This is often intended for public resources.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** informational / high / manual_verification_required
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** Responses to requests without an Origin header returned Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** Behaviour for real cross-origin requests; credentialed access (browsers forbid '*' with credentials, and that header's value is redacted); that the data is sensitive.
- **Remediation:** Return Access-Control-Allow-Origin only for origins that need access, unless the resource is intentionally public.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** none
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-CLNT-07 Testing Cross Origin Resource Sharing
- **CWE:** none

## SV-HDR-001: HSTS missing or ineffective on HTTPS responses (v1)

HTTPS responses from this origin had no Strict-Transport-Security header, or one that is invalid or has max-age=0.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** low / high / automated_detection
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** The observed HTTPS responses had no Strict-Transport-Security header, or it had max-age=0 or an invalid value.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That downgrade or stripping attacks are feasible; HSTS preload status; the behaviour of pages that were not fetched.
- **Remediation:** Send Strict-Transport-Security with a positive max-age on all HTTPS responses.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** none
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-CONF-07 Test HTTP Strict Transport Security
- **CWE:** none

## SV-HDR-002: No enforced Content-Security-Policy on HTML responses (v1)

Successful HTML responses from this origin had no enforced Content-Security-Policy header (a report-only policy does not count).

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** low / high / automated_detection
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** The observed HTML responses had no enforced Content-Security-Policy header (report-only or no header).
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That any injection (XSS) exists; policies delivered through <meta> tags; the quality of any policy that is present.
- **Remediation:** Define a Content-Security-Policy suited to the application and send it on HTML responses.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** none
- **WSTG v4.2:** none
- **CWE:** none

## SV-HDR-003: No framing protection on HTML responses (v1)

Successful HTML responses from this origin had neither X-Frame-Options (DENY/SAMEORIGIN) nor a Content-Security-Policy frame-ancestors directive.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** low / high / automated_detection
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** The observed HTML responses had neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That a page offers sensitive one-click actions; that clickjacking is practical; JavaScript frame-busting.
- **Remediation:** Send Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (or 'none'), and/or X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** none
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-CLNT-09 Testing for Clickjacking
- **CWE:** CWE-1021 Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

## SV-HDR-004: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff missing (v1)

Successful responses from this origin lacked X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** informational / high / automated_detection
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** The observed responses lacked X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That content-type sniffing is exploitable; that user-controlled content is served.
- **Remediation:** Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all responses.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** none
- **WSTG v4.2:** none
- **CWE:** none

## SV-INF-001: Software version disclosed in response headers (v1)

A Server, X-Powered-By, X-AspNet-Version or X-AspNetMvc-Version header contained a version-like string.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** informational / high / automated_detection
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** A header advertised a product name with a version-like string.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That the version is accurate (headers can be spoofed or added by proxies) or vulnerable; no CVE matching is done.
- **Remediation:** Remove or genericise version information in response headers.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** none
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-INFO-02 Fingerprint Web Server
- **CWE:** CWE-497 Exposure of Sensitive System Information to an Unauthorized Control Sphere

## SV-INF-002: Error or stack-trace text in a response (v1)

The stored response excerpt contains text that matches documented error or stack-trace markers of common platforms.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** low / medium / manual_verification_required
- **Subject:** endpoint
- **PROVES:** The stored (at most 2 KiB by default, redacted) excerpt contains text matching documented error or stack-trace patterns.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That sensitive internals are exposed; that the error is attacker-triggerable; that injection exists; anything beyond the stored excerpt.
- **Remediation:** Return generic error pages to clients and log details server-side; disable debug modes outside development.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** A10:2025 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-ERRH-01 Testing for Improper Error Handling
- **CWE:** CWE-209 Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

## SV-INF-003: Directory listing page (v1)

A successful HTML response matched documented auto-index markers such as a title starting with 'Index of /'.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** low / medium / automated_detection
- **Subject:** endpoint
- **PROVES:** A response matched documented directory-index markers (for example a title 'Index of /...').
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That the listed files are sensitive or downloadable; listing on other paths.
- **Remediation:** Disable automatic directory indexes on the web server.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** none
- **WSTG v4.2:** none
- **CWE:** CWE-548 Exposure of Information Through Directory Listing

## SV-MTH-001: Potentially risky methods advertised in Allow (v1)

An OPTIONS response advertised PUT, DELETE, TRACE, CONNECT or PATCH in its Allow header. The Allow header often does not reflect what is actually enabled.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** low / low / manual_verification_required
- **Subject:** endpoint
- **PROVES:** An OPTIONS response's Allow header listed PUT, DELETE, TRACE, CONNECT or PATCH.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That those methods are implemented, enabled, unauthenticated or harmful. No such request is ever sent by the scanner.
- **Remediation:** Disable methods the application does not need and make sure the Allow header is accurate; verify manually in an authorized test.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** none
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-CONF-06 Test HTTP Methods
- **CWE:** none

## SV-TRN-001: Application served over cleartext HTTP (v1)

Responses from this origin were delivered over unencrypted HTTP.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** low / high / automated_detection
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** The origin served the scanned responses over unencrypted HTTP at scan time.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** That sensitive data is transmitted; that HTTPS is unavailable; that traffic can be intercepted on the real network.
- **Remediation:** Serve the application over HTTPS only and redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** A04:2025 Cryptographic Failures
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-CRYP-03 Testing for Sensitive Information Sent via Unencrypted Channels
- **CWE:** CWE-319 Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

## SV-TRN-002: TLS certificate could not be verified (v1)

With certificate verification enabled, the TLS handshake to this origin failed certificate verification.

- **Severity / confidence / detection:** low / high / manual_verification_required
- **Subject:** origin
- **PROVES:** With verification on, the TLS handshake to this host and port failed certificate verification against the scanner host's trust store.
- **DOES NOT PROVE:** Which defect it is (self-signed, expired, wrong name, unknown CA); that users' browsers would distrust it; that interception is possible; anything about protocol or cipher strength.
- **Remediation:** Inspect the certificate. If the service is meant to be trusted by clients, serve a valid certificate for this hostname from a CA those clients trust.
- **OWASP Top 10:2025:** none
- **WSTG v4.2:** WSTG-CRYP-01 Testing for Weak Transport Layer Security
- **CWE:** none
